title: Pointcept/PTv3 GOOSE baseline cannot start on Apple Silicon — no CUDA path exists
dataset: GOOSE 3D validation split, archive downloaded 2026-08-22 from goose-dataset.de
sensor_configuration: Velodyne Alpha Prime 128-channel roof LiDAR only, as distributed in the annotated archive
annotation_schema: Published baseline reports on the GOOSE 8-class challenge taxonomy; the downloadable validation archive ships 64-class labels/ only, with no labels_challenge/ directory
model: Pointcept fork FraunhoferIOSB/Pointcept branch goose, PTv3 backbone, pretrained weights challenge_ptv3.pth

environment.hardware: Apple M4. No NVIDIA GPU, no CUDA device, and none is possible on this architecture.

error: docker --version -> 'command not found: docker'; nvidia-smi -> 'command not found: nvidia-smi'; python -c 'import torch' -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'; uname -sm -> 'Darwin arm64'; cpu brand -> 'Apple M4'
attempted_fixes: Checked whether the documented install path could start at all. goose_dataset/pointcloud_processing/README.md instructs 'cd Pointcept/scripts && ./build_image.sh', a Docker image tested against CUDA_VERSION=11.7 and CUDNN_VERSION=8.
Confirmed Docker is not installed on this machine.
Confirmed no NVIDIA GPU is present. Installing Docker would not help: Apple Silicon has no CUDA capability, so the image cannot run regardless.
Stopped rather than installing Docker, which would not have changed the outcome.
blocker: The published baseline is distributed only as a CUDA 11.7 Docker image. Apple Silicon cannot execute CUDA under any configuration, so this is a hardware incompatibility rather than a setup problem, and no amount of local configuration resolves it.
recommendation: Reassign to Ricky's Windows machine (GTX 1660, 6 GiB, CUDA 12.6) as task R7, with Google Colab's T4 as the fallback. Before investing in either environment, resolve the annotation-schema mismatch recorded above: the published 0.8096 mIoU is on the 8-class challenge taxonomy and the downloadable archive has no labels_challenge/ directory, so a 64-to-8 mapping must be found or derived first. If neither environment works, this becomes the project's documented answer on running an off-the-shelf model locally.
notes: Recorded as a first-class result per DZ-3 rather than discarded. Risk R-08 anticipated exactly this, and Adrian said at kickoff that 'we spent X number of days trying to get it going, we couldn't get it going' is a reportable outcome. Time-boxed at 0.2 hours because the blocker was architectural and identifiable before any install was attempted — the useful discipline here was checking prerequisites first rather than debugging a build for a day. The published 0.8096 mIoU is retained as reference context in NEXT-STEPS.md, not as a measurement produced by this failed local run.
